keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 27-29: after Liu Yong's death at Suiyang in 27 only his son Liu Yu's Tanhai Commandery stood: 'during August AD 29, Liu Yu's Tanhai Commandery was captured'. Linyi (Shandong) stands for Tanhai, which lay round Tan; the page does not place it.

ledger.note: 23: Liu Yong is named Prince of Liang. 'Liu Yong was named the Prince of Liang and Suiyang (Liang Commandery) was his capital'; he soon 'began to act independently' of the Gengshi Emperor.
25: Liu Yong proclaims himself emperor. 'In AD 25, after Emperor Gengshi was defeated by the Chimei Army, Liu Yong proclaimed himself emperor'. Same state, prince to emperor.

Liu Yong 'attacked Jiyin, Shanyang, Pei, Chu, Huaiyang, and Runan Commanderies, gaining 28 cities'; the page dates none of these conquests, so they are entered at the proclamation year (confidence 1). notes:
Liu Yong, the Liang of Suiyang 23-29. 2 pages opened (Liu Yong (Xin dynasty), Emperor Guangwu of Han); no Cliopatria row. Not the Liu Yong (Three Kingdoms) page.
Unsettled: (1) the six-commandery conquest (28 cities) has no date on the page (confidence 1 at 25); (2) the Yuzhou, Yanzhou, Qingzhou and Xuzhou 'part of the Commandery area' is not mapped beyond Shangqiu and Xuzhou circles; (3) the page gives Liu Yong's death as 27 (no month) and Liu Yu's last stand at Tanhai to August 29 (Tanhai placed by Linyi, not by the page); (4) Dong Xian, Prince of Haixi, named with Zhang Bu in spring 27, has no dossier and no region on the page.
Counterparts: han-dynasty and lulin exist (ea-02-c); zhang-bu is written by this batch.
